items.checklist_text: Run `charness tool doctor nose --no-write-locks` before installing `nose` and confirm missing `nose` reports `doctor_disposition: advisory-install-needed`, not a blocking install failure.
items.precondition_note: The checklist says `before installing nose`. `nose` was already installed for this entire session, so the literal pre-install state was never occupied. A PATH-scoped stand-in was SUBSTITUTED to reach the missing arm. Graded the same way item 5's unmet precondition is graded; v2 inconsistently graded this one plain `executed`.

commands.command: env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin $(command -v charness) tool doctor nose --no-write-locks

items.finding: This checklist expectation is FALSE, and the refutation is executed rather than inferred. PATH-scoping reproduces the missing arm without uninstalling anything, and the observed disposition is `blocking-install-needed` — precisely what the checklist says must not occur. Mechanism, stated with the step v2 omitted: scripts/doctor_lib.py runs a `doctor_status` ladder FIRST (lines 220-231), in which a missing support sync would win and route to `blocking-support-sync-needed` (line 240). That branch is unreachable for `nose` specifically because it declares no `support_skill_source`, so `inspect_support_sync` returns `not-tracked` (scripts/support_sync_lib.py:59-67) — corroborated by item 6's own `skipped` result. With that branch excluded, the disposition ladder reaches line 238 `advisory-install-needed` only if `install_route.mode == 'manual'` OR `doctor_policy == 'advisory'` (condition at line 237); integrations/tools/nose.json declares `doctor_policy: required` (:77) with `mode: script` (:16), so the assignment at line 242 `blocking-install-needed` is what remains. `blocking-failure` (line 244) requires a successful detect and is not reachable here.
items.tag_time_check: `git show v6.0.0:integrations/tools/nose.json` reports the same `doctor_policy: required` and `mode: script`, so this was already true at tag time and is not post-release drift. Executed by the parent; no transcript captured for this one command.
items.disposition: RESOLVED after this record was first written: the checklist text was the defective surface and has been corrected. `integrations/tools/README.md` permits `doctor_policy: advisory` ONLY where the consuming workflow has an explicit degraded path; `nose` declares `access_modes: [binary]` and its own `degradation.when_missing` says doc near-duplicate review has NO fallback, so `required` is correct and relaxing it was not available. The `checklist_text` above is preserved as the text these seven items were EXECUTED against, not as current adapter content.

non_claims: This record preserves observations; it is not a release-success verdict.
`origin/main` is ahead of tag v6.0.0, so nothing here re-verifies the published v6.0.0 tree.

No `commands[].value` in this file is verbatim stdout. Every one is an author-selected extract; the named transcript is the re-checkable artifact. Transcripts were captured on a re-run, not during the original executions, and `charness update` has no transcript at all — the one command the adapter explicitly asks to record as executed proof.

The item-1 correction is scoped to the MANAGED SOURCE CHECKOUT. It does not claim the plugin roots are unclosable without a push — those have a documented local-sync route which was deliberately not run.
Three surfaces the same install path writes were NOT measured (Codex plugin cache, Claude wrapper, installed CLI binary). `surfaces.measured` is three of at least six.
Nothing here establishes that a push WOULD close the managed-checkout skew; that is an inference from path attribution plus the pull-only sync mode, not an executed proof.

Item 2's missing-`nose` state was PATH-SIMULATED, not actually absent. The refutation establishes that a missing `nose` reports `blocking-install-needed` on THIS host at THIS commit; it does not decide whether the adapter checklist or the doctor policy should change.
Item 3 ran a SUBSTITUTED command (`--detail` added); the adapter's literal `--dry-run` does not print what the item asks to confirm.
The manifest-supported nose install path is unexecuted; only the dry-run plan and the pre-existing binary's version were observed. The item-5 detection is therefore not an after-install observation.
Item 1's third command compares an installed EXPORT against repo SOURCE, unlike the export-vs-export recursive diffs; it is not an independent drift observation.
Items 2-6 resolved repo_root to the managed checkout ~/.agents/src/charness (at origin/main); item 7 ran against the unpushed dev tree. This is not one uniform host surface.
The `cited-check == repo-gate spot check` reading in item 1 is the author's; the adapter does not define the phrase.
